messages.subject: overlapping layer, with different data
parts:
Hi list,


I'm sure that it is a very simple response but I need some advice.

How can I overlay layer of different data.set? I have a geom_line + geom_path into one graph using data.set.1 (see code below), my interest is overlapping stat_contour that use other data.set


# -----------------------------

rm(list=ls())


library(ggplot2)

library(reshape)

library(reshape2)

library(KernSmooth)


# data <- dget('kobe_data.txt')

# see data below code


# first graph ----------------------------------------------

dta <- data[[1]] # fishing mortality and spawning biomas

v <- data[[2]] # Reference points {F20%, F40% and SBo}

F20 <- v[1]

F40 <- v[2]

F40.F20 <- F40/F20

So <- v[3]

yymax <- 1.4*max(dta$Ft,F40.F20)


kobe <- ggplot(dta, aes(x = SB/v[3], y = Ft/v[1])) +

theme_bw() + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1)) +

scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,yymax),

breaks = round(sort(c(0.5,1.0,F40.F20,1+(F40.F20-1)/2,yymax-(yymax-F40.F20)/2)),digits = 3),

labels = c(' 0.5','1.0',paste(round(1+(F40.F20-1)/2,digits=2)),

expression(F[20]/F[40]),paste(round(yymax-(yymax-F40.F20)/2,digits=2))))


kobe <- kobe +

geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 1.0, ymin = 0.0, ymax = yymax, fill = 'yellow', alpha = 0.015) +

geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 0.4, ymin = 1.0, ymax = yymax, fill = 'red', alpha = 0.015) +

geom_rect(xmin = 0.4, xmax = 1.0, ymin = 1.0, ymax = 0.0, fill = 'green', alpha = 0.035) +

geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 0.2, ymin = F40.F20, ymax = yymax, fill = 'red', alpha = 0.15) +

geom_path(linetype = 2, size = 0.3) + geom_point(aes(size = yr,fill = yr), shape = 21) +

scale_size(range=c(0,5)) +

labs(y = 'Mortalidad por pesca, relativa a F40%',

x = 'Fracción de la Biomasa Virginal', colour = 'Año', size = 'Año', fill = 'Año') +

scale_fill_gradient(limits=c(dta$yr[1], dta$yr[length(dta$yr)]), low="black", high="#FF9326")+ # colour = yr

geom_text(data = head(dta,1), label = dta$yr[1], colour = 'black', vjust = 2, size = 3)


print(kobe)


# second graph [including 'simulated' uncertainty for 2010] -------------------------------------

x.mcmc <- dta$SB[33]/v[3]*rlnorm(100,0,0.01)

y.mcmc <- dta$Ft[33]/v[1]*rlnorm(100,0,0.01)


bw = 25

levs = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95)


bwx = (max(x.mcmc) - min(x.mcmc))/bw

bwy = (max(y.mcmc) - min(y.mcmc))/bw

est <- bkde2D(cbind(x.mcmc, y.mcmc), bandwidth = c(bwx, bwy), gridsize = c(51,51))

tmp.1 <- expand.grid(x = est$x1, y = est$x2)

tmp.2 <- melt(est$fhat)

tmp.3 <- data.frame(x=tmp.1$x, y=tmp.1$y, z=tmp.2$value)


# this is OK

fr <- ggplot(tmp.3,aes(x=tmp.3$x, y=tmp.3$y, z=tmp.3$z))

fr + stat_contour()


# SEE HERE ----------------------------------

# but I can't get any graph

kobe + stat_contour(tmp.3,aes(x=tmp.3$x, y=tmp.3$y, z=tmp.3$z))


# -------------------- end code --------------------------------------------------------


Thanks a lot

messages.subject: Re: overlapping layer, with different data
parts:
Hi:

In ggplot2, if you define x and y a particular way in ggplot(), it is
expected that those variables will be used for x and y in *all*
subsequent layers, which is why you couldn't get the contours to plot.
The workaround is not to define those variables in the ggplot()
statement but to assign them in the geom calls instead (see
geom_path(), geom_point() and geom_text() below).

Here's one way to get what you asked for, but I don't think it's what
you expected....

ggplot(dta) +
theme_bw() +

geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 1.0, ymin = 0.0, ymax = yymax,
fill = 'yellow', alpha = 0.015) +
geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 0.4, ymin = 1.0, ymax = yymax,
fill = 'red', alpha = 0.015) +
geom_rect(xmin = 0.4, xmax = 1.0, ymin = 1.0, ymax = 0.0,
fill = 'green', alpha = 0.035) +
geom_rect(xmin = 0.0, xmax = 0.2, ymin = F40.F20,
ymax = yymax, fill = 'red', alpha = 0.15) +

geom_path(aes(x = SB/v[3], y = Ft/v[1]), linetype = 2, size = 0.3) +
geom_point(aes(x = SB/v[3], y = Ft/v[1], size = yr, fill = yr), shape = 21) +

scale_size(range=c(0,5)) +
labs(y = 'Mortalidad por pesca, relativa a F40%',
x = 'Fracción de la Biomasa Virginal',
colour = 'Año', size = 'Año', fill = 'Año') +
scale_fill_gradient(limits=c(dta$yr[1], dta$yr[length(dta$yr)]),

low="black", high="#FF9326") + # colour = yr
geom_text(data = head(dta, 1), aes(x = SB/v[3], y = Ft/v[1]),

vjust = 2, size = 3) +
geom_contour(data = tmp.3, aes(x = x, y = y, z = z)) +

scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1)) +
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,yymax),
breaks = round(sort(c(0.5,1.0,F40.F20,1+(F40.F20-1)/2,
yymax-(yymax-F40.F20)/2)),digits = 3),
labels = c(' 0.5','1.0',
paste(round(1+(F40.F20-1)/2,digits=2)),
expression(F[20]/F[40]),

paste(round(yymax-(yymax-F40.F20)/2,digits=2))))

That little splotch of blue around the 2010 point is your contour
plot. You can zoom in on it with coord_cartesian(), but I needed to
get rid of the scale_continuous() calls in order to do that.

One thing you could do would be to create the contour plot separately,
absent the legend and titles, save it at a suitable size, and then use
annotation_raster() or annotation_custom() to insert it into the main
plot as an inset. If you wanted, you could create a small rectangle
around the 2010 point to indicate the position of the contour in the
main plot, perhaps with a line pointing to it from the inset using
geom_segment() with an optional arrow. A couple of examples using
annotation_raster() and annotation_custom() are in the 0.9.0
transition guide:
http://cloud.github.com/downloads/hadley/ggplot2/guide-col.pdf See
section 4.

HTH,
Dennis
